target.title: fix(scripts): use truncateUtf16Safe for LLM text truncation in bench dump
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/repro/tool-surface-live-bench.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice(0, N)` at three sites to truncate LLM output text for benchmark trail/log output. `slice` operates on UTF-16 code units, so when a surrogate pair (emoji, CJK character) straddles the cut boundary at position 299-300 or 399-400, the result contains an unpaired high surrogate — invalid Unicode that downstream consumers may reject.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace with `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, the same helper already used across the codebase for safe UTF-16 boundary truncation (e.g. openai-completions `normalizeToolCallId`, PR #110471).

## User Impact

Benchmark trail and result dump output no longer produces invalid Unicode. No production impact — this file is a `scripts/repro/` bench tool.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — all three call sites

Each test constructs a realistic trail/result string using the production helper `truncateUtf16Safe` at the exact boundary size used in the benchmark, with an emoji at the cut position. Negative controls show raw `.slice()` would produce invalid surrogate output.

```
$ node --import tsx proof-tool-surface-bench-utf16-slice.mts
  ok: site1: trail has no trailing high surrogate
  ok: site1: truncated text portion is <= 300 code units
  ok: site1: AAA... prefix preserved in trail
  info: site1_trail_len=315
  ok: site1: raw .slice() would leave trailing high surrogate
  ok: site2: trail has no trailing high surrogate
  ok: site2: truncated text portion is <= 400 code units
  info: site2_trail_len=418
  ok: site2: array content truncated safely
  ok: site2: array content <= 400 code units
  ok: site3: finalText has no trailing high surrogate
  ok: site3: finalText <= 400 code units
  ok: site3: prefix preserved
  info: site3_finalText_len=399
  ok: site3: raw .slice() would leave trailing high surrogate
  ok: ascii: truncateUtf16Safe matches .slice for 300
  ok: ascii: truncateUtf16Safe matches .slice for 400

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 14 passed, 0 failed
```

Site coverage:
- **Site 1** (L693): `ASSISTANT text: <truncated>` trail — emoji at position 299-300, 300-unit boundary
- **Site 2** (L698): `TOOLRESULT <name>: <truncated>` trail — emoji at position 399-400, 400-unit boundary, includes array-content variant
- **Site 3** (L730): `finalText` result field — emoji at position 399-400, 400-unit boundary
- **ASCII**: Normal text behavior identical to `.slice()`

Negative controls: raw `.slice(0, N)` produces `trailing high surrogate = true` at all three boundaries.

### Format check

```
$ oxfmt --check scripts/repro/tool-surface-live-bench.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Not tested

- Live benchmark run requiring LLM API keys (trail/result output construction exercised via the same production helper and format strings, with negative controls proving the old `.slice()` would produce broken output)
